newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee praises Deng's spirit, courage.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee praises Deng's spirit, courage.

text.p: Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's spirit and courage never failed, and he helped set the stage for China to become a heavyweight nation, Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew said.

In a letter to Chinese President Jiang Zemin released late on Thursday, Lee, Singapore's prime minister from 1959 to 1990, said Deng fought against oppression by warlords and against the Japanese occupiers in World War Two, and suffered great hardships during the Cultural Revolution.
"Next, he told me he was shoved out by the Gang of Four in 1976. But his spirit and courage never failed," Lee said.
He said Deng brought China to its present progress with his Open Door Policy in 1978.
"He saved China. Without him, China could have been like the Soviet Union. Instead China will become a huge heavyweight nation in 30 years," Lee said.
Deng died late on Wednesday from respiratory failure. He was 92.
Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said earlier on Thursday that he was saddened by Deng's death, but said the legacy of the paramount leader would be a "strong and prosperous China".
"I am saddened to learn of Deng Xiaoping's demise," Goh said in a statement.
Goh, who met Deng several times, described him as one the world's great leaders who "saw events in historical sweep, and thought in terms of generations".

Singapore President Ong Teng Cheong, in a letter to Jiang, said, "China has lost a wise leader who had vision and the courage to implement it" and who "contributed to the peace and prosperity of the region and of the world."
Despite its small size, Singapore has been a major investor in China, with Lee and other leaders encouraging the city state's companies to expand activities there.

The government's Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Thursday it was confident investments in China would keep growing despite Deng's death. The EDB said Singapore was the fifth largest investor in China, with total investment amounting to US$1.86 billion in 1995.
